sources.title: ATO: General interest charge (GIC) rates
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 4 September 2026): GIC annual and daily rates: October to December 2026 11.51% (0.03153425%); July to September 2026 11.43% (0.03131507%); April to June 2026 10.96% (0.03002740%). Section 8AAD of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 specifies how the rate is calculated; the daily rate is the annual rate divided by the days in the calendar year. Rates for the next quarter are generally announced 2 weeks before it starts.
sources.limitations: Quarterly rates change. Verify the rate for each day of the period at use time.

sources.title: ATO: Shortfall interest charge (SIC) rates
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: SIC annual and daily rates: October to December 2026 7.51% (0.02057534%); July to September 2026 7.43% (0.02035616%); April to June 2026 6.96% (0.01906849%).
sources.limitations: Read from the page's published table without its last-updated date. Quarterly rates change; verify each quarter at use time.

sources.title: ATO: Penalty units
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 26 June 2026): Penalty unit amount by date the infringement occurred: $364 on or after 1 July 2026; $330 from 7 November 2024 to 30 June 2026; $313 from 1 July 2023 to 6 November 2024. Penalties are not deductible.
sources.limitations: Verify the value for the infringement date at use time.

sources.title: ATO: Failure to lodge on time penalty
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 22 June 2026): Base penalty: one penalty unit for every 28 days or part thereof that the document is overdue, up to 5 penalty units, for individuals and small withholders. Multiplied by 2 for a medium withholder, 5 for a large withholder and 500 for a significant global entity, tested in the month the document was due. Generally no penalty notice for a late return or activity statement that results in a refund or nil, with stated exceptions. Remission criteria and the registered agent safe harbour are set out on the page.
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, the withholder definitions and PS LA 2011/19 at use time.

sources.title: ATO: Denying deductions for ATO interest charges
sources.fact: Read 26 September 2026 (page last updated 8 June 2026). GIC and SIC incurred on or after 1 July 2025 are not deductible for income years starting on or after that date, whatever year the debt relates to, and a later remission of such an amount is not assessable. GIC or SIC incurred before 1 July 2025 remains deductible for 2024-25 and earlier years, and a later remission of a deducted amount is assessable. An entity with a substituted accounting period loses the deduction from its next accounting period starting after 1 July 2025. GIC on unpaid income tax is incurred daily; SIC is incurred in the year the amended assessment notice is served.
sources.limitations: ATO summary of the law change. Confirm the provisions of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Incentives and Integrity) Act 2025 for the period at use time.
